text: 🇲🇽🏭 "Next year it can be paid without any fine, without any surcharge, for any amount." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, 50th anniversary of the Business Coordinating Council (CCE), Mexico City, Oct 13, 2026 Sheinbaum announced that in 2027 anyone with debts to the tax authority can settle them without fines or surcharges, with no limit. She listed agreements reached with business: a year and a half of capped gasoline and diesel prices against inflation, the sugar deal with the US, wage increases, the 40-hour week, bank accounts without a tax ID up to four times the old limit, and a single window that approves investment projects within 60 days. "There will be things we don't agree on, but let us always put above everything what we do agree on."
banner: TAX DEBTS: NO FINES, NO SURCHARGES

text: 🇲🇽🛢️ "Any development project has to have local benefits." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 14, 2026 Residents of San Luis de la Paz, Guanajuato, a municipality with a strong Indigenous identity, oppose a solar park owned by an Italian company. They cite water shortages and broken promises on reforestation and jobs. Sheinbaum said an environmental and social impact assessment is mandatory for any energy project, and companies must talk with the communities. She recalled her own academic research on wind farms in the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, which found that much of it had been built "through dispossession or low rents."

🇲🇽✊ "So much time paying rent, I could never have that peace of mind, as a single mother with children to raise." — Catalina Álvarez, new homeowner, Playa del Carmen, Mañanera, Oct 14, 2026 Catalina works as a cleaner at a cinema and paid up to 6,000 pesos a month in rent. Today she received the keys to a Well-being Housing home in Playa del Carmen, Quintana Roo, where Infonavit is delivering all 288 homes of the Puerto Maya development. "Many people say: 'no, at my age I won't make it.' It can be done." Infonavit director Octavio Romero reported 45,100 homes delivered in 27 states so far. Quintana Roo's goal is 62,000 homes, and 29,000 are already contracted.

🔥🇲🇽 "Very opportunistic, frankly, to say the least." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 14, 2026 Asked about Workers' Party (PT) figures who joined Tuesday's march by IMSS health workers, Sheinbaum showed a drone image of the march taken from social media "so that each person can do their own count." She said the workers' legitimate demands will be met: IMSS director Zoé Robledo must deliver an action plan this week, missing medicines are being restocked, and raises for residents' stipends and job security for staff hired during COVID are being worked out. She asked that today's union vote on the IMSS offer be completely free. She also pointed to the use of the legitimate demand by some organizations, right-wing outlets and bot accounts.

🇲🇽✊ "The Sembrando Vida program continues, and it will go on for the entire six-year term." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 14, 2026 Sheinbaum addressed planters who had written to her worried that the program would end. Created by López Obrador in 2019, Sembrando Vida planted more than 1.2 billion native trees between 2019 and 2025, according to Agriculture Secretary Columba López. It pays 414,080 planters, 138,000 of them women, 6,450 pesos a month, on more than a million hectares, about seven times the size of Mexico City. The goal for 2024–2030 is 1.5 billion more trees; 129 million have been planted so far this year. It is now run jointly by the Well-being, Environment and Agriculture ministries.

🇲🇽📱 <u>AT&T Leaves Mexico: Televisa and David Martínez Buy It for $2 Billion</u>

AT&T is exiting Mexico's mobile market after 11 years. A 50-50 consortium of Grupo Televisa and David Martínez's Fintech Holdings will buy AT&T México for $2 billion, El Economista reports. It is the country's second-largest mobile carrier, with 24.7 million subscribers, 85.4 billion pesos in 2025 revenue and just 1.4 billion pesos in operating profit. The deal still needs regulatory approval and should close in the first quarter of 2027.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Chihuahua: PRI and PAN Threaten Electoral Councilors Over a Gender-Parity Rule</u>

Chihuahua's electoral institute (IEE) drafted gender-parity guidelines for the 2026-2027 election, including a measure requiring parties to run only women in 23 municipalities. State PRI leader Alejandro Domínguez is pushing impeachment of the councilors, and the PAN is weighing a bid to remove them. Morena's representative said impeachment is a constitutional tool, but brandishing it as a public warning is pressure on the electoral authority.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>Veracruz Bets on Native Maize: 100 Tractors, 5 Seed Houses, 10 Milk Centers</u>

Governor Rocío Nahle's government set up five native-maize seed houses and bought 100 tractors, plus harvesters, lending them free to farmers who work 1 to 10 hectares. Ten new milk collection centers supply Liconsa, which pays guaranteed prices, and the Bienestar ministry will buy Veracruz maize for the Tiendas del Bienestar. "When we saw that we had to work to help the president with food sovereignty, we focused on maize," Nahle said.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Huachicol Fiscal: Senate Sets Fines of Up to 100% of the Cargo's Value</u>

The Senate approved the president's Customs Law reform 66–37, over opposition protests. Fuel and petroleum imports with irregular paperwork will now be fined 50% to 100% of their commercial value. The reform also scraps the 50% threshold that kept customs from seizing undervalued shipments when the price gap was smaller. It takes effect January 1, 2027.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mexico and the US Freeze a Cártel del Noreste Network That Funded Election Campaigns</u>

Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF) and the US Treasury acted together: the bank accounts and assets of four people and 11 companies tied to the Cártel del Noreste are now frozen. The businesses ranged from quarter-horse racing to construction, trucking, and oil and gas. According to OFAC, one of them, Construcciones y Edificaciones Garza Elías (Cegesa), funneled cartel money into election campaigns and won government contracts through corruption.
